Commercial codec route and exact mel contract for pinned IndicF5 (fb652a9)
#48
by rb440 - opened 25 minutes ago
Discussion
rb440
25 minutes ago

Hello AI4Bharat team,

We are validating an offline internal commercial film/drama/dubbing integration against ai4bharat/IndicF5 at fb652a96e508091045890dae5bb99fe511facbcf. We have not loaded weights or generated speech, and have not enabled a commercial runtime.

The selected source uses the Vocos mel path. The public pip vocos 0.1.0 dependency includes encodec 0.1.1, whose published license is CC BY-NC 4.0. We are keeping the full codec-rights gate closed rather than inferring that an MIT model card licenses every dependency or checkpoint.

We compared only the exact pinned source get_vocos_mel_spectrogram/get_bigvgan_mel_spectrogram CPU functions, with an authored one-second 24 kHz sine and their defaults (100 mel channels, hop 256). Vocos produced [1,100,94]; BigVGAN produced [1,100,93]. Mean absolute difference over the 93 common frames was 3.221302032470703. This is a preprocessing diagnostic, not a speech or decoder-quality benchmark, and we have not cropped/padded a model output or claimed checkpoint equivalence.

Could you confirm:

A publisher-supported commercially permitted vocoder/code/checkpoint stack for this exact IndicF5 revision, including its immutable source/model revisions and license scope?
Whether a BigVGAN route is supported for this trained checkpoint, and the normative frontend normalization, frame alignment, mel range, sample rate and decoder checkpoint? Matching 24 kHz alone is insufficient.
Whether model.safetensors embeds vocoder state and requires the original Vocos architecture/key layout, or a separately validated conversion is required?

We also saw discussion #43 concerning pretraining provenance and would appreciate a publisher response there; this request concerns the distinct codec/preprocessing compatibility issue. No private scripts, voice recordings, credentials or production assets are included. Thank you.

Pinned modular component revisions for distilled checkpoint (59e4141)
#3
by rb440 - opened 36 minutes ago
Discussion
rb440
36 minutes ago

We are validating only model-free integration of Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers@59e4141466bcb1bf9733eca1bc78be6891c9fbdf; no checkpoint weights were downloaded or loaded.

The original Diffusers PR #14412 lacked the two named distilled modular exports. We found the official merged PR https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14413 and tested its immutable merge commit 3a2f35d4efa4c059c8bfb3bc0d6c906264895c81. Both WanAnimate2DistilledModularPipeline and WanAnimate2DistilledBlocks now import, and ModularPipeline.from_pretrained(local_metadata_dir, local_files_only=True, trust_remote_code=False) successfully constructs the original pinned modular index without loading components.

The remaining reproducibility question is that the published index has null revisions for several components and refs/pr/1 for scheduler/transformer (previously resolved to ff28d41a9c0c331137691847cc8700593d785593). Could you confirm the intended immutable component revisions for this exact checkpoint, including whether those PR component tensors are equivalent to the pinned main checkpoint?

The merged implementation defines WanAnimate2VideoProcessor and its own CLIP preprocessing, whereas the old monolithic index declares CLIPImageProcessor. Please confirm that the merged modular preprocessing is the normative contract for these exact weights and whether a revised, fully revision-pinned modular index is available. We are keeping model execution disabled until the component mapping and runtime acceptance are verified.
